overview.tagline: Missouri landmarks → Memphis music and history
overview.subtitle: Twelve days of public destinations with synthetic personal details.
overview.route: Sacramento → St. Louis → Saint Charles → Cape Girardeau → Memphis → home

days.mission: Spot the Gateway Arch from the airplane window.
days.funFact: The Gateway Arch is 630 feet tall and 630 feet wide.
days.highlight: Touch down in St. Louis and settle in downtown.
headsUp: Allow at least 15 minutes after landing for bags before heading to the rental-car shuttle.
Downtown hotel garages often cost extra; confirm overnight rates and check SUV height clearance.
Keep the first evening deliberately light in case the flight or baggage runs late.
All booking details in this demo are invented.

days.mission: Ride the tram to the top of the Arch.
days.funFact: The Arch's tram system combines features of an elevator and a Ferris wheel.
days.highlight: Gateway Arch, museum, riverfront, then Saint Charles.
headsUp: Open mobile tickets before entering the security line in case reception is weak.
Arrive at least 30 minutes before the tram reservation for parking, walking, and security.
GPS can be confusing near the riverfront; use the attraction's official arrival directions.
The tram capsules are small and enclosed; review accessibility information before the visit.
Check official hours and ticket policies again on the morning of the visit.

days.mission: Find a Lewis and Clark reference along the riverfront.
days.funFact: Saint Charles served as Missouri's first state capital.
days.highlight: Historic Main Street and Missouri River history.
headsUp: Historic Main Street includes brick and uneven surfaces; comfortable shoes help.
Leave room in the schedule to wander—the riverfront, shops, and historic buildings are close together.
Check museum hours before committing to an indoor stop; some historic sites keep limited schedules.

days.funFact: Public Fourth of July celebrations in the United States date back to 1777.
days.highlight: A slower holiday near the riverfront.
headsUp: Major attractions and roads can be packed on the holiday; the slower Saint Charles plan avoids much of the city-center crush.
If City Museum becomes the backup plan, arrive at opening and expect holiday crowds.
Bring water, hearing protection for sensitive kids, and a simple exit plan for fireworks.
Holiday hours and event locations change; verify current details that morning.

days.funFact: Cottleville was incorporated in the nineteenth century.
days.highlight: A fictional family celebration preserving the app's event-day pattern.
headsUp: Set out event clothes and anything the family needs the night before.
Allow a 15–20 minute drive plus a buffer for parking and finding the entrance.
Confirm dress code, start time, and whether the main gathering is indoors or outdoors.
The venue, people, and timing in this public demo are synthetic.

days.mission: Find a favorite panel on the riverfront floodwall murals.
days.funFact: Cape Girardeau's riverfront murals illustrate regional history.
days.highlight: Drive south and explore the Mississippi riverfront.
headsUp: Vacation-rental checkout times can be strict; finish the host checklist before loading the final bags.
Keep water and sun protection handy—the riverfront murals have limited shade.
This is a transition day, so avoid packing the afternoon too tightly if checkout runs late.

days.mission: Stand near the microphone used in early rock-and-roll recordings.
days.funFact: Sun Studio is associated with early recordings by Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, and Jerry Lee Lewis.
days.highlight: Sikeston lunch, Sun Studio, and Beale Street.
headsUp: Sun Studio: 706 Union Avenue, Memphis, TN 38103 · (901) 521-0664.
Tours can sell out and the historic studio is small; check the current schedule before driving over.
The National Civil Rights Museum is normally closed on Tuesdays, which is why this itinerary places it later in the week.
Memphis heat in July can exceed 90°F; carry water and schedule outdoor walking in shorter blocks.
Beale Street changes character later at night, so choose timing that fits the group.

days.mission: Find a favorite stage costume at Graceland.
headsUp: Graceland: 3764 Elvis Presley Boulevard, Memphis, TN 38116.
Arrive well before the tour window for parking, ticket pickup, security, and the shuttle to the mansion.
Do the outdoor portions early when possible; the afternoon heat can be draining.
The complex is larger than the mansion tour alone—leave time for cars, aircraft, exhibits, and food.
Use the official website for current entry, bag, accessibility, and parking instructions.

days.mission: Choose one story from the museum to discuss over dinner.
days.funFact: The National Civil Rights Museum incorporates the historic Lorraine Motel.
days.highlight: Civil Rights history in downtown Memphis.
headsUp: National Civil Rights Museum: 450 Mulberry Street, Memphis, TN 38103.
Allow several hours; the museum carries a lot of historical and emotional weight and is best experienced without rushing.
I AM A MAN Plaza is beside Clayborn Temple at 294 Hernando Street.
This day connects the Lorraine Motel with the 1968 Memphis sanitation strike and the workers' “I AM A MAN” campaign.
Talk with children beforehand about what they may see and leave space to discuss it afterward.

days.mission: Ride the glass elevator to the Lookout and spot the Mississippi River from above.
days.funFact: The Memphis Pyramid is 321 feet tall and is one of the world's tallest pyramids.
days.highlight: Stax Museum in the morning · Bass Pro Shops at the Pyramid after lunch.

adventures.name: Stax Museum of American Soul Music
Bass Pro Shops at the Pyramid
Beale Street or BBQ — flex night

headsUp: Stax Museum: 926 East McLemore Avenue, Memphis, TN 38106.
The Bass Pro Shops Pyramid is at 1 Bass Pro Drive; observation-deck and attraction tickets cost extra.
The Pyramid has a large surface lot, but confirm current parking fees on arrival.
Stax is more rewarding if everyone listens for how gospel, blues, country, and rhythm and blues combine into Memphis soul.

days.mission: See the Peabody ducks make their famous walk.
days.funFact: The Peabody duck tradition began in the 1930s.
headsUp: The Peabody Duck March is traditionally at 11:00 AM; arrive around 10:30 for a better view and verify the current schedule.
Mason Temple: 930 Mason Street, Memphis, TN 38126.
For Mud Island, use the north entrance and parking area or walk the Skybridge from downtown for river views.
At Mud Island, explore the lower Mississippi River scale model, the large MEMPHIS sign, and the river overlooks.
Weigh suitcases before bed so departure morning stays calm.

days.mission: Choose one favorite memory from the trip.
days.funFact: A structured itinerary can make travel details easier to find without removing flexibility.
days.highlight: Pack, return the car, and fly home.
headsUp: Confirm hotel checkout, rental-car return, and flight times together the night before.
Plan to reach the terminal about 90 minutes before a domestic flight, with extra time for the rental-car shuttle.
Keep fuel, luggage, and any rental-car inspection time in the departure buffer.
Download boarding passes and keep one final-day essentials bag easy to reach.
Flight times and confirmation codes in this public demo are synthetic.
